report.source_text: Physical examination revealed a middle-aged man, not in apparent distress but who appeared confused and could not provide his own history. Scars from previous staples were seen near the right scapular region. Skin examination was significant for a dark red papular skin rash in the right thoracic area roughly at the fourth and fifth intercostal areas (dermatomal T2 and T3 distribution) extending to posterior axilla where multiple hard lumps were palpated in groups. Lesions were tender with purulent discharge (Figures 1, 2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old man with a history of resected cutaneous melanoma of the right scapular area and incomplete chemotherapy presented with a dark red papular rash and tender, purulent lesions with palpable lumps on the right thoracic area in a T2-T3 dermatomal distribution. A skin biopsy of these lesions demonstrated cells positive for melanoma markers S-100 and Melan-A and negative for epithelial marker CK AE1/AE3, supporting melanoma cell involvement. Imaging studies were ordered but no results were disclosed. The clinical presentation combined with histopathologic findings confirms metastatic amelanotic melanoma at the right thoracic skin.
